sections.content: North Las Vegas, Nevada has quietly become one of the most compelling real estate investment markets in the entire Southwest. While the Las Vegas Strip gets all the headlines, savvy investors are locking in deals just a few miles north — where prices are lower, population growth is real, and rental demand keeps climbing. Whether you're new to investing or a seasoned wholesaler looking for your next market, this guide covers everything you need to find profitable real estate deals in North Las Vegas NV. If you're just getting started, check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving in.
North Las Vegas Market Overview

North Las Vegas is a separate city from Las Vegas proper, covering roughly 100 square miles with a population approaching 300,000. It sits just north of downtown Las Vegas in Clark County and has been one of the fastest-growing cities in the United States over the past decade. Major employers include Amazon, Nellis Air Force Base, and a growing roster of logistics and manufacturing companies drawn by Nevada's business-friendly tax environment. That economic engine creates consistent housing demand — which is exactly what real estate investors want to see. You can explore current inventory and deal activity at our [North Las Vegas market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/north-las-vegas-nv).
Average Home Prices in North Las Vegas

As of 2024, the median home price in North Las Vegas sits around $340,000 to $360,000, which is noticeably lower than the broader Las Vegas metro median of roughly $420,000. Entry-level single-family homes in older neighborhoods can still be found in the $250,000 to $290,000 range, while newer construction in master-planned communities pushes toward $400,000 and above. For investors, that spread creates real opportunity — especially for those targeting distressed properties or off-market deals below the median. Days on market has hovered around 30 to 45 days for move-in ready homes, while distressed properties tend to sit longer, giving wholesalers and flippers more negotiating room.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors
Not every zip code in North Las Vegas performs the same way, and knowing where to focus your search can make or break your returns. Here are the areas that consistently attract investor attention.

items: Aliante (89084): A master-planned community with strong rental demand, newer homes, and low vacancy rates. Great for buy-and-hold landlords.
Carey & Simmons Corridor (89030, 89031): Older stock with more distressed inventory and lower price points — ideal for wholesalers and flippers looking for value-add plays.
Eldorado (89081): Working-class neighborhood close to major employers. Strong blue-collar rental demand and affordable acquisition costs.
Craig Ranch (89032): Mid-tier suburban area with good schools and stable owner-occupant demand. Solid for fix-and-flip with exit strategy to retail buyers.
Civic Center District (89030): Closest to downtown Las Vegas, undergoing revitalization. Higher risk but potentially higher upside for investors willing to be patient.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Focus your first deals in Aliante or Craig Ranch if you want lower risk and faster exits. Once you know the market, the older 89030 and 89081 zip codes offer deeper discounts and bigger spreads for experienced investors.
Types of Deals Available in North Las Vegas
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is active in North Las Vegas thanks to a steady supply of distressed properties, probate situations, and absentee landlords who bought during the pre-2008 boom and never returned to manage their properties. Assignment fees in this market typically run between $10,000 and $25,000 on deals where ARV ranges from $280,000 to $380,000. To build your wholesale pipeline here, focus on driving for dollars in the 89030 and 89081 zip codes, pulling pre-foreclosure lists from the Clark County recorder's office, and sending direct mail to out-of-state owners. If you're new to this strategy, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide walks you through the entire process step by step.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

North Las Vegas has a strong fix-and-flip environment. Labor costs in Nevada are moderate compared to coastal markets, and the permitting process through the City of North Las Vegas is generally faster than in Clark County unincorporated areas. A typical light rehab (cosmetic updates, new flooring, kitchen refresh) on a 3-bed, 2-bath home runs $25,000 to $45,000, while a full gut renovation might run $60,000 to $90,000. Flippers targeting the $300,000 to $380,000 resale price range see the most buyer activity. Always run your numbers before committing — use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate after-repair value based on comparable sales in the specific zip code.
Rental Properties

The rental market in North Las Vegas is one of the strongest arguments for buying and holding here. Average rents for a 3-bedroom single-family home range from $1,500 to $1,900 per month depending on condition and location. Vacancy rates remain below 5% in most neighborhoods, driven by the influx of workers from new distribution and manufacturing facilities. Cash-on-cash returns of 6% to 9% are achievable for investors who buy right, especially on deals sourced off-market. Nevada is also a landlord-friendly state with no rent control at the state level and a relatively streamlined eviction process, making it attractive for long-distance landlords.
Local Market Trends to Watch

items: Population growth: North Las Vegas added over 20,000 residents between 2020 and 2023 and shows no signs of slowing, driven by California migration and job creation.
Industrial expansion: The Apex Industrial Park north of the city continues to attract major employers, which pushes workforce housing demand higher.
Interest rate impact: Higher mortgage rates have softened retail buyer competition, which is good news for investors — sellers are more motivated and days on market have increased.
New construction pressure: DR Horton and KB Home are active in North Las Vegas, creating competition for retail flips in the $380,000+ range. Keep exit prices realistic.

Short-term rental demand: Clark County regulations on STRs are stricter inside Las Vegas proper, but North Las Vegas has its own permitting process — check current rules before banking on Airbnb income.

Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

North Las Vegas attracts a significant number of California, Washington, and Arizona investors who want Nevada's tax advantages without paying Las Vegas strip-area prices. If you're investing from out of state, here's how to approach this market without getting burned.

items: Build a local team first: Find a reliable property manager, a real estate-focused contractor, and a local title company before you put your first deal under contract. Ask in local REIA groups for referrals.

Verify ARV with local comps: National AVMs like Zillow often overestimate values in rapidly shifting Nevada markets. Pull your own comps from the Clark County Assessor's data or use a local agent to verify.

Use a deal calculator before every offer: Run every deal through our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to make sure your MAO (Maximum Allowable Offer) leaves enough margin for profit and contingencies.

Target off-market properties: The best deals rarely hit the MLS. Learn how to source them directly using strategies covered in our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).

Understand Clark County vs. City of North Las Vegas: Permitting, zoning, and property taxes are administered differently depending on whether the property is within city limits or in unincorporated Clark County — confirm jurisdiction early.
Analyze deals conservatively: Out-of-state investors often underestimate holding costs and management fees. Add a 10% buffer to your estimated rehab costs and assume a 60-day flip timeline minimum.

sections.content: Pro Tip: One of the fastest ways to learn a new market remotely is to analyze 20 to 30 deals before making a single offer. Use our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to build that analytical muscle before you commit real capital.
Is North Las Vegas Right for You?

North Las Vegas offers a rare combination of affordable entry prices, strong rental demand, landlord-friendly laws, and an economy that keeps adding jobs and residents. It's not a get-rich-quick market — but for investors who do their homework, source deals carefully, and manage numbers conservatively, it can be a very consistent performer. Wholesale spreads are real, flip margins are workable, and rental yields beat most coastal alternatives by a wide margin. The key is knowing where to look, how to analyze what you find, and how to build reliable local relationships that give you access to deals before they go public.
